constraints: a single monomial fraction over another; invert and multiply; coefficients at most 12
hints: A fraction over a fraction is division, so leave the top monomial fraction in place and invert the lower one.
Multiply after the reciprocal step, then use quotient-of-powers rules to reduce the x-factors.
Reduce numerical coefficients and write any remaining variable exponents positively, respecting x not equal to zero.

constraints: a proportion with a linear binomial in at least one part; cross-multiply, then solve a linear equation; integer solutions
hints: A proportion can be cleared by multiplying each numerator by the opposite denominator.
Write the cross-products with parentheses around any binomial numerator.
Expand, solve the resulting linear equation, and verify no original denominator becomes zero.

constraints: two or three terms with monomial or linear-binomial denominators; the cleared equation is linear; solutions may be fractions
hints: Record values that make each denominator zero before manipulating the equation.
Multiply every term by the least common denominator so no fractions remain.
Solve the cleared linear equation and test the candidate in the original denominators.

constraints: the cleared equation has a root at an excluded value
hints: Factor or identify the denominator restriction before cancelling a common factor.
Solve the cleared equation, but keep track of the value that was excluded by the original denominator.
Test the algebraic roots in the original rational equation and label the valid and excluded values in the requested roles.
